regression_flag.finding: REGRESSION FLAG (per round-2 locked protocol clause 2): gigi-embedded p50 grows 0.9 us -> 1.5 us -> 1.6 us across 10k -> 100k -> 1M (1M/10k ratio 1.78x; p95 1.2 -> 2.4 -> 2.6 us, 2.17x). Not flat, therefore flagged, not smoothed. Decomposition as measured: nearly all growth is in the 10k->100k decade (1.67x); the 100k->1M decade is 1.07x (near-flat over 10x more rows, within rep-to-rep spread: 100k reps p50 1.4/1.5/1.9, 1M reps 1.6/1.5/2.1). The absolute delta is ~0.7 us at sub-2 us latencies — a shape consistent with working-set/cache-hierarchy effects rather than an O(log N) or O(N) index — but the protocol requires the growth be reported as a regression finding, and it is.

disclosures: EXPERT PARITY: gigi was granted exactly the SQL author's domain knowledge — cohort = (merchant x 2h bucket), amount = value channel — and nothing else. Labels were never sent to gigi.
Both candidate plays are reported with their measured PR-AUCs; the best is labeled best. No cherry-picking.

The expert bundle carries two client-derived fields (cohort, amount_sq) computed during UNTIMED ingest prep; the SQL arm computes its bucket inside the timed query. The wall-time asymmetry favors gigi and is disclosed; the derivation's LOC is priced into every play's LOC (as the SQL arm's CAST was inside ANOM_SQL).
PLAY 1 weights ({context:cohort: 1.0}) are fixed a priori from the granted knowledge, not fitted — /scan/fit was NOT used (it needs labels, which the protocol withholds).

PLAY 1's context:cohort lens is gigi's cohort-local curvature kappa=|amount-mu|/range z-scored within cohort then rank-normalized globally — the granted knowledge in gigi's idiom, not a verbatim z-score reimplementation.

PLAY 2 computes the per-row |z| client-side from server-side INTEGRATE moments (GQL has no stddev aggregate — round-1 finding stands); population-stddev convention identical to the SQL arm; zero-variance cohorts score 0 like the SQL arm's COALESCE.
The round-1 zero-config /scan cell is carried verbatim as anomaly_zero_config_round1 (PR-AUC 0.0848 as measured in round 1).
All expert cells measured over HTTP at 127.0.0.1:3143 (gigi's real deployment shape), persistent keep-alive, strictly serial.

honest_summary: EMBEDDED INGEST (schema-parity re-run, post-audit): gigi in-process ingests 116,526 rows/s median at 100k (reps 116,526/121,503/109,554, .index('txn_id') maintained inside the clock like every other system) — 1.5x faster than its own HTTP shape (78,775) but still LOSES to in-process sqlite (617,285, 5.3x) and duckdb (390,428, 3.4x). Removing HTTP closes part of the gap, not the gap. The pre-fix no-index figure (134,381) is retained as superseded context only.

EMBEDDED POINT QUERY: p50 1.5 us / p95 2.4 us at 100k — 37x faster than in-process sqlite (55.5 us round-1 / 68.8 us this sweep) and 236x faster than gigi's own HTTP shape (353.7 us round-1). Round 1's point-query loss was the transport, not the engine.

SCALING p50 10k->100k->1M: gigi-embedded 0.9 -> 1.5 -> 1.6 us (1.78x, REGRESSION-FLAGGED per protocol — growth concentrated in 10k->100k at 1.67x, 100k->1M near-flat at 1.07x; sub-us absolute deltas, shape consistent with cache effects, flagged anyway); gigi-HTTP 381 -> 410 -> 427 us (1.12x, near-flat — transport floor dominates, supports O(1) within jitter); sqlite 56.6 -> 68.8 -> 72.5 us (1.28x p50; p95 grows 2.25x, 93 -> 209 us — B-tree log-N visible). No system's curve is perfectly flat; embedded gigi is 45-63x faster than in-process sqlite at every N measured (62.9x at 10k, 45.9x at 100k, 45.3x at 1M) — noting the embedded side is a native-Rust timing loop vs Python's sqlite3 wrapper (protocol shape, disclosed).

EXPERT-PARITY ANOMALY (same domain knowledge as the SQL author, labels never sent): PLAY 2 (GQL INTEGRATE cohort moments + client |z|) PR-AUC 0.7189 — EXACTLY TIES expert SQL 0.7189, in 53.5 ms vs sqlite 33.6 ms, 21 LOC vs 15. PLAY 1 (weighted cohort-lens /scan, gigi's own idiom) PR-AUC 0.7003 — close but BELOW expert SQL (-0.0186), in 287.9 ms. Both reported; best is PLAY 2. The round-1 gap (0.0848 vs 0.7189) was the knowledge, not the engine: granted the same cohort structure, gigi reaches parity via GQL and near-parity via its native lens. The native /scan idiom still gives up 1.9 pts of PR-AUC and 8.6x wall time vs the SQL baseline (287.9 vs 33.6 ms; 5.4x vs gigi's own PLAY 2 at 53.5 ms) — the interaction-lens roadmap gap from round 1 stands, narrowed but real.

PLAY 2 ties SQL by construction to the extent the math is the same statistic (population z per cohort); the honest reading is that GQL can EXPRESS the expert's statistic at comparable line-count, not that gigi found something SQL could not.
